t: Lesson 7, agents and subagents.
Your instructor is Patrick Diamitani.
This is where you stop typing and start leading.
Describe the software you want in plain language, typed or spoken, and AI agents write the code.
With subagents, you can hand the work to a whole team of them.
One agent doing everything gets slow and confused, instead hand pieces to specialists.
One researches, one builds, one reviews.
Each works in its own clean context, so the main thread stays sharp.
An agent is another markdown file.
It has a role and a list of tools it may use.
Then its instructions.
This reviewer can read but never edit.
Delegating well means writing a good brief.
The goal and why it matters.
What done looks like.
What not to touch.
And what to report back.
Put it together.
Approve the plan.
Let agents build in parallel.
Have the reviewer and the tests check the work.
Then push to get and deploy.
Quick recap.
You lead, specialist agents build, each in a clean context.
You review.
Your mission.
Create one reviewer agent and run it after your next change.
You lead, they build, you review.
Next lesson, rolling this out to a whole team.
